analyst_view.overall: Early view: Ararat-Armenia (bottom, 0 points, 14 conceded) host NEC in Yerevan's national stadium, and the goalkeeper Joao Bravim and Bruno Wilson, both listed as missing, should be available again after serving their bans at Salzburg, unless UEFA adds to Bravim's red card. NEC (12th, 7 points) have taken seven points from their last three European games under Dick Schreuder, though they are only 11th in the Eredivisie.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Ararat's games have averaged 4.5 goals and NEC's 4.25, with NEC scoring seven in their last two European games (4-2 at Dinamo, 3-1 against Omonia). Ararat have scored in three of four, so both teams scoring in a high total looks the likeliest shape.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.9 of them for NEC. That fits a game NEC should control, with Tjaronn Chery's set pieces a regular source of chances, so I stay close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Ararat have picked up a red card and a three-yellow ban in this league phase, but with nothing left to play for by then the edge may go out of their game; the two pull in opposite directions.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Ararat's open games and NEC's attacking approach under Schreuder fit a high total, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. I lean a little higher: Ararat have let in 14 goals in four games, which points to a lot of clear chances conceded, and Dusan Tadic and Bryan Linssen have been finishing well for NEC.
